title: The diner re-cooks: ecology works travel as provenance-locked Quick Snacks
editorial_proposition: A standing reuse relation transcribed retroactively (2026-07-17): six works of the ecology — one Ensemble premiere, five Meridian instruments — are re-served on data-snack.com as Quick Snacks whose per-file provenance frontmatter (supplier, work, gauntlet, inspected) is a delivery slip that predates this ledger; the transport automation exists but is deliberately only part-armed; one open correction is recorded (wing language in the supplier template). The relation is open and running.

proposition_author.note: retroactive transcription commissioned by Frank (2026-07-17); lean record — the nightly scribe appends from here

status.statusLine: open/standing — 14 works re-cooked (three new: STILL DARK, ALL AT ONCE and NOT YET, published 2026-09-02 in commit e03327a — the first successful auto-publish since 2026-07-29's 11th work), but the 34-run publish stall was interrupted, not resolved: run #55 (2026-09-02) succeeded only because the persistently-blocking upstream work (field-research's 2026-07-26-unable-to-ring-its-own-bell) happened to hit a transient model-provider demand-limit error on that one run and fell through the pipeline's generic skip path instead of its usual hard "no sources cited" fail, so the exit-code guard never tripped — the very next scheduled run (#56, 2026-09-03) reached the same sources check again and failed it again, byte-identically, discarding a larger six-item batch unpublished (the-second-reader; corrections to native-speaker, still-dark, all-at-once and not-yet; and a new premiere, "THE SAME NUMBER TWICE"); a further, previously-unseen fault surfaced on run #55's own successful publish: the downstream "Deploy to Cloud Run" step failed on a GCP bucket-permission error ("forbidden from accessing the bucket [data-snack_cloudbuild]"), so whether the three newly-published snacks are actually live on data-snack.com is an open question this record cannot resolve from CI history alone; none of this fixed, flagged, or reacted to anywhere but the workflow's own run history; four open corrections carried forward unchanged (wing-language; one-tap's still-unreacted-to source kill; the recurring silent re-voicing pattern; the publish-stall pattern itself, now shown to be interruptible by chance rather than repaired)
